title: Infer request provenance and adjust quotas for cross-tenant cache fusion
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: When multiple tenants' requests are fused into a single inference microbatch and some tokens are served from prefix/KV cache, our current billing pipeline attributes token costs inconsistently. In practice we either (A) bill the entire microbatch to a single owner or (B) prorate based on post-hoc token expansion heuristics. Both approaches lead to incorrect quota debits and confusing rate-limit enforcement (e.g., a tenant sees quota depletion even though most tokens were answered from cached state).

Goal: Introduce a lightweight provenance tagging model at ingress and an aggregation rule for billing that ensures each tenant is charged only for their effective non-cached token compute and is subject to fair rate-limits. This should work across: hosted API multi-tenant microbatches, Dedicated tenant-colocated batching, and future Private multiplexed pools.

Scope: Add request_provenance metadata, emit a cache_hit_vector on response, change billing job to compute effective_token_charge per request owner before applying quota/rate limit and emitting usage events. Backfill not required for historical reporting; new metrics are forward-looking.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress service attaches a stable request_provenance id and owner tag to every request before batching.
Serving runtime emits cache_hit_vector (binary per-token/segment) and a condensed cache_summary (prefetch_hit_count, kv_hit_count) per request.
Billing pipeline consumes provenance + cache hints and produces an effective_token_charge for each original request owner.
Quotas and rate limiter apply charges derived from effective_token_charge and reject requests correctly under the same time-window semantics as today.
End-to-end test harness demonstrates correct billing for 5 canonical scenarios (all-cached, none-cached, mixed-interleaved, speculative-prefetch, cross-tenant-fusion).
Performance: additional metadata adds <3% p99 tail to ingress path and billing job latency remains within SLA with a 10% CPU headroom margin.
tasks: Design: finalize provenance schema and minimal cache hint format (Ava)
Ingress: attach provenance id + owner fields to requests (Ravi)
Runtime: emit per-request cache_summary and optional token-level cache_hit_vector (opt-in flag) (SRE/Runtime)
Billing: update aggregation logic to compute per-owner effective_token_charge from batch and cache hints (Billing team)
Rate limiter: consume effective_token_charge and ensure same-window enforcement semantics (Throttling team)
E2E tests: add simulated microbatch fusion tests and monte-carlo billing checks (QA)
Bench: measure metadata overhead on p95/p99 tail, iterate (Perf)
Docs: update Metering docs and Console cost breakdown to surface effective_token_charge (Docs)
Launch: staged rollout on a subset of production traffic + monitoring dashboards (Ops)
implementation_notes: Provenance model: use 128-bit UUID (request_provenance) + owner_id (account_id) + request_shard_index to map microbatch subrequests post-fusion.
Cache hints: keep cache_summary compact (3 ints: prefix_hits, kv_hits, served_from_cache_flag) and only enable token-level cache_hit_vector behind a debug flag to limit bandwidth.

Billing change: compute effective_token_charge = max(0, nominal_token_count - cached_token_equivalent). nominal_token_count comes from tokenization at ingress; cached_token_equivalent estimated from cache_summary using deterministic rules to avoid reprocessing token streams.

Rate-limiting: apply quota debit at the moment of computed charge emission. Keep existing sliding-window semantics; treat cached tokens as zero-cost but still account for request frequency for DDOS detection (separate throttle metric).
Telemetry: emit metrics: billing.effective_token_charge, billing.cache_fraction_by_owner, rate_limit.declines_by_owner, ingress.provenance_attach_failures.
Backwards compatibility: for components that do not yet produce cache hints, fall back to conservative per-request nominal charging but mark usage with meter.inferred=true for later reconciliation.
Storage: store per-request effective_token_charge in usage_events stream for downstream billing and Console dashboards.
rollout_plan: Week 1: feature-flagged deploy of ingress provenance tagging to 10% of nodes + unit tests
Week 2: runtime emits cache_summary to 10% traffic; billing job reads summary but still uses legacy path (dry-run) and emits diagnostics
Week 3: enable billing path to apply computed effective_token_charge behind feature flag for 5% customer traffic; monitor deltas against legacy accounting
Week 4: expand to 50% if deltas within threshold (<0.5% variance for non-cache-heavy customers), otherwise iterate
Week 5: global rollout and documentation update; remove dry-run; run reconciliation job for the first 7 days to detect anomalies
comments: 2026-03-02 - Ava Martinez: Spike completed. Verified that prefix cache hits are the largest source of ambiguity because they shrink token sequences without clear owner boundaries. Prototype attached in the PR link above.
2026-03-04 - Ravi Kapoor: Implemented ingress tagging. Bench shows +0.8% p95 latency on tagging path. Lowered metadata size by compressing owner_id to 8 bytes.

2026-03-06 - SRE (Jin Park): Runtime change emitted cache_summary for debug traffic. Observed that speculative-prefetch flows report overlapping prefix hits across owners; will need deterministic tie-break rule in billing.

2026-03-08 - Billings (María Gomez): Proposed deterministic attribution rule: attribute shared prefix cache saves proportionally to nominal token counts unless owner requests mark shared segments as private. Pending PM sign-off.
2026-03-10 - PM (Noah Li): Approved deterministic attribution as interim rule with a follow-up to add request-level signals for private/shared cache semantics.
2026-03-12 - Ravi Kapoor: Billing dry-run comparison on 1M requests: median effective charge delta 0.4% vs legacy, tail differences concentrated in 2 customers (investigating).
2026-03-14 - Ava Martinez: Decision: enable partial rollout week 3 behind feature flag. Action items: add reconciliation alert for any tenant with >5% negative delta post-cutover.
